```{r}
library(knitr)
library(car)
library(psych)
library(emmeans)
library(effectsize)
```

# Wide formatted data

```{r}
# Load wide data
Lab10Wide = read.table("Lab10Data_wide.csv",
                       sep = ",",
                       header = T)

kable(Lab10Wide, align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

# Long formatted data (same values as above)

```{r}
# Load long data
Lab10Long = read.table("Lab10Data_long.csv",
                       sep = ",",
                       header = T)

Lab10Long$Subject = factor(Lab10Long$Subject)
Lab10Long$Hemisphere = factor(Lab10Long$Hemisphere)
Lab10Long$Time = factor(Lab10Long$Time)

kable(Lab10Long, align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

```{r}
# "contr.sum" is the correct option for type III SS
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
```

# One-way repeated measures (Time) on only left hemisphere data

## Descriptives
```{r}
# Use left hemisphere columns only, treated as the single group
describe(Lab10Wide[,2:5])
```


```{r}
Lab10OneWayLM = lm(cbind(Left10, Left20, Left30, Left40) ~ 1,
                   data = Lab10Wide)

idata_one = data.frame(Time = factor(c("10", "20", "30", "40")))

a_one = Anova(Lab10OneWayLM, idata = idata_one, idesign = ~ Time, type = 3)

summary(a_one, multivariate = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# How the GG and HF corrections work.
# 1) You multiply any df in your omnbimus by the epsilon value. In this case 
# your variable of interest and the error term.
df_time_GG  = 3 * 0.4956
df_error_GG = 21 * 0.4956

df_time_HF  = 3 * 0.5982211
df_error_HF = 21 * 0.5982211

# 2) Plug in the F you have and the new df to get your new p, which is already 
# printed in the summary above. Below is a fuller demonstration.

# p-values with the adjusted dfs (F = 199.063 from the omnibus)
print("Manually calculated p-value for GG correction")
pf(199.063, df_time_GG, df_error_GG, lower.tail = FALSE)
print("Manually calculated p-value for HF correction")
pf(199.063, df_time_HF, df_error_HF, lower.tail = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# You don't need to recalculate your various SS or MS values, becuase the df scales all the values the same way. This means that the top and bottom of the fraction that gives you F have both been scaled the same way. For example,if you multiply the top and bottom of 1/4 by 3, you still have 1/4.

# Full demonstration of the corrections (reuses the dfs above).
SS_time  = 7774.125
SS_error = 273.375

# Greenhouse-Geisser
MS_time_GG  = SS_time  / df_time_GG
MS_error_GG = SS_error / df_error_GG
F_GG        = MS_time_GG / MS_error_GG

# Huynh-Feldt
MS_time_HF  = SS_time  / df_time_HF
MS_error_HF = SS_error / df_error_HF
F_HF        = MS_time_HF / MS_error_HF

print("Second Manually calculated p-value for GG correction")
pf(F_GG, df_time_GG, df_error_GG, lower.tail = FALSE)
print("Second Manually calculated p-value for HF correction")
pf(F_HF, df_time_HF, df_error_HF, lower.tail = FALSE)

```

### Partial eta-squared (Time) SSTime/(SSTime + SSError)

```{r}
# Use the correct variables from above to calculate partial eta for time.

partialEta_Time = 1/1

print("Manual")
print (partialEta_Time)

eta_squared(a_one)
```



```{r}
# A model using long data is necessary for post hoc comparisons.
Lab10OneWayLong = Lab10Long[Lab10Long$Hemisphere == "Left", ]

Lab10OneWayLongLM = lm(CBFV ~ Time + Subject, data = Lab10OneWayLong)

```



### Post hoc comparisons (no need for simple effects)

Bonferroni
```{r}
emm_time_one = emmeans(Lab10OneWayLongLM, ~ Time)
kable(summary(pairs(emm_time_one, adjust = "bonferroni")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

LSD (equal to none)
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emm_time_one, adjust = "none")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

Tukey
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emm_time_one, adjust = "tukey")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
```


# Two-way repeated measures (Hemisphere x Time)
## Descriptives

```{r}
describe(Lab10Wide[2:9])
```

```{r}
Lab10LM = lm(cbind(Left10, Left20, Left30, Left40, Right10, Right20, Right30, Right40) ~ 1,
             data = Lab10Wide)

idata = expand.grid(Time = factor(c("10", "20", "30", "40")),
                    Hemisphere = factor(c("Left", "Right")))

a = Anova(Lab10LM, idata = idata, idesign = ~ Hemisphere * Time, type = 3)
summary(a, multivariate = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Partial eta-squared
# Hemisphere
partialEta_Hemisphere = 1/1

# Time
partialEta_Time = 1/1

# Hemisphere x Time
partialEta_Hemisphere_Time = 1/1

print("Manual Hemisphere")
print(partialEta_Hemisphere)

print("Manual Time")
print(partialEta_Time)

print("Manual Hemisphere x Time")
print(partialEta_Hemisphere_Time)

eta_squared(a)
```

```{r}
# Effect size using emmeans function.
Lab10LongLM = lm(CBFV ~ Hemisphere * Time + Subject, data = Lab10Long)
```

Bonferroni
```{r}
emm_hemi = emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Hemisphere)
emm_time = emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Time)

kable(summary(pairs(emm_hemi, adjust = "bonferroni")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
kable(summary(pairs(emm_time, adjust = "bonferroni")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

LSD (equal to none)
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emm_hemi, adjust = "none")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
kable(summary(pairs(emm_time, adjust = "none")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

Tukey
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emm_hemi, adjust = "tukey")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
kable(summary(pairs(emm_time, adjust = "tukey")), align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

## Pairwise follow-ups for the interaction
### Multiple t-tests of Hemisphere at each level of Time (only two levels of Hemisphere, so no simple-effect ANOVA required)

Bonferroni
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Hemisphere | Time), adjust = "bonferroni")),
      align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

LSD (equal to none)
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Hemisphere | Time), adjust = "none")),
      align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

Tukey
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Hemisphere | Time), adjust = "tukey")),
      align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

## Simple effect follow-ups for the interaction
### Time has more than two levels, so pairwise comparisons among Time at each level of Hemisphere require a significant simple effect. Because Time is repeated, each simple effect is a one-way RM ANOVA.

```{r}
# Simple effect of Time at Left Hemisphere
# (reprint of the one-way omnibus already run above)
a_one$univariate
```

```{r}
# Simple effect of Time at Right Hemisphere
Lab10RightLM = lm(cbind(Right10, Right20, Right30, Right40) ~ 1,
                  data = Lab10Wide)

idata_right = data.frame(Time = factor(c("10", "20", "30", "40")))

a_right = Anova(Lab10RightLM, idata = idata_right, idesign = ~ Time, type = 3)
summary(a_right, multivariate = FALSE)
```

## Pairwise follow-ups for the interaction
### Multiple t-tests of Time at each level of Hemisphere (uses the error term from the model)

Bonferroni
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Time | Hemisphere), adjust = "bonferroni")),
      align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

LSD (equal to none)
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Time | Hemisphere), adjust = "none")),
      align = 'c', digits = 3)
```

Tukey
```{r}
kable(summary(pairs(emmeans(Lab10LongLM, ~ Time | Hemisphere), adjust = "tukey")),
      align = 'c', digits = 3)
```
